# Philadelphia 76ers vs Cleveland Cavaliers Prediction, Odds and Betting Tips

**NBA | October 22, 2026 | Regular Season | 7:00 PM ET**  
**Venue:** Wells Fargo Center, Philadelphia

**Prediction:** Philadelphia 76ers Moneyline  
**Odds:** 1.74  
**Implied break-even probability:** 57.47%

| Team | Game venue | 2026/27 record through Oct 21 | Points for | Points against |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Philadelphia 76ers | Home | 1-0 | 106 | 100 |
| Cleveland Cavaliers | Away | 0-0 (season opener) | not yet available | not yet available |

**Settlement:** Full-game moneyline; overtime included.

## Match assessment

Philadelphia opened the 2026/27 season with a 106-100 road win over New York on October 20, led by 28 points from Tyrese Maxey, 19 from Jaylen Brown and 14 from LeBron James, while Joel Embiid added 13 points and 11 rebounds. That is the only game-level evidence available for either side: Cleveland play their first regular-season game of the new campaign here, so a 2026/27 Cleveland scoring average cannot yet be meaningfully calculated and is not estimated from an earlier season.

The tactical question for Philadelphia is whether their perimeter scoring depth (Maxey, Brown and James all in double figures in the opener) can be sustained at home while Embiid continues to anchor the defensive glass. Cleveland center Jarrett Allen was listed as questionable with a knee issue in a pregame update; his participation should be treated as uncertain rather than assumed either way heading into Cleveland's own opener.

Philadelphia's moneyline at 1.74 refers to the full-game winner, including overtime, under conventional NBA rules. The price implies a 57.47% break-even threshold before the bookmaker's margin. A single opening game cannot validate that rate on its own, particularly against a visitor that has not yet played a 2026/27 regular-season game and whose own form is simply unknown at this point. Late injury news, foul trouble and three-point variance are the clearest downside risks to the selection.

*Statistics are from the clubs' actual 2026/27 season-opening results, not an assumed carryover from 2025/26. Cleveland's figures are marked not yet available rather than estimated, since the Cavaliers have not played a 2026/27 regular-season game as of this editorial update.*
